cards.task: Use the key to open the door, then reach the goal.

wrong.why: Takes the key and opens the door, then never reaches the goal.

cards.notes: Task text: first task of examples/arm-fm/minigrid-doorkey/tasks.json. Pilot bundle generated from this text. Changed in card fix 2: the key-before-door and door-before-goal orders are forced by the world, so they are optional extras in scoring (`forced`); Existence(at_goal) alone is also a correct output. S2 2026-11-19: the Response chain with the first trigger required (Response(first, door_open), Response(door_open, last), Existence(first)) is also a correct output (`also_ok`), the same alternative the pilot and smoke copies of this card already carry. Order audit 2026-11-20: the task states both orders ("use the key to open the door", "then reach the goal"), and a stated order is required even when the level forces it, so `forced` is gone and Existence(at_goal) alone is no longer correct. The Response chain stays `also_ok`: it states both orders as "after a, b". Card fixes 2026-11-20: the Response chain left `also_ok` too. `Response` is not a step form, so it does not carry the stated orders (user rule); the pilot and smoke copies lost it the same day.

cards.task: Acquire the matching key, unlock the door, and pick up the designated box in the other room.

wrong.why: Takes the key and opens the door, then never picks up the box.

cards.notes: Task text: first task of examples/arm-fm/minigrid-unlock-pickup/tasks.json. Pilot bundle generated from this text. The agent carries one object, so it drops the key before taking the box. Changed in card fix 2: the key-before-door and door-before-box orders are forced by the world, so they are optional extras in scoring (`forced`); Existence(target_picked_up) alone is also a correct output. S2 2026-11-19: the Response chain with the first trigger required (Response(first, door_open), Response(door_open, last), Existence(first)) is also a correct output (`also_ok`), the same alternative the pilot and smoke copies of this card already carry. Order audit 2026-11-20: both orders stay `forced`. The task lists the steps with no order word ("Acquire ..., unlock ..., and pick up ..."), so it states no order; the same reading makes "Open the door and pick up the box" two goals. This is the closest call of the audit; the pilot and smoke copies of this card require both orders. Stated-order rule 2026-11-20 (user): only order words ("then", "after", "before") give an order, so this plain list is three facts. `expect` is one Existence per fact, the ordered chain (the old `expect`) is the `also_ok` answer, and `forced` is gone. The Response chain left `also_ok`: it is neither the facts nor the chain, and `Response` is not a step form (the base-doorkey ruling). The chain with all three Existences is also accepted (second `also_ok`): it equals the chain; the extra Existences are implied (MONA: same LTLf; same states and transitions, only the hard-break and end charges grow).

cards.task: Pick up the blocking ball and the key, in either order, unlock the door, and then pick up the box in the other room.

wrong.why: Clears the ball, takes the key and opens the door, then never picks up the box.

cards.notes: Task text: first task of examples/arm-fm/minigrid-blocked-unlock-pickup/tasks.json. The first drop must leave the door reachable. Changed in card fix 2: the wording now says the ball and the key may come in either order (the example task text keeps the ball-first list), because a key-first run satisfies every clause; the three orders are forced by the world, so they are optional extras in scoring (`forced`) and Existence(target_picked_up) alone is also a correct output. Order audit 2026-11-20: the list "..., unlock the door, and then pick up the box" states all three orders (the ball and the key before the door, the door before the box), and a stated order is required even when the level forces it, so `forced` is gone and Existence(target_picked_up) alone is no longer correct.

cards.task: Explore the side rooms, find and acquire the key matching the locked target room, return to the corridor, open the target door, and pick up the designated object.

wrong.why: Takes the key and opens the target door, then never picks up the object.

cards.notes: Task text: first task of examples/arm-fm/minigrid-key-corridor/tasks.json. Navigation opens closed unlocked side doors on the way. Changed in card fix 2: the key-before-door and door-before-object orders are forced by the world, so they are optional extras in scoring (`forced`); Existence(target_picked_up) alone is also a correct output, and the card does not measure exploration. Order audit 2026-11-20: both orders stay `forced`. The task lists the steps with no order word, so it states no order (the same reading as base-unlock-pickup). The stated "find and acquire the key" has no clause in `expect`; listed for review. Card fixes 2026-11-20: no change. "Find and acquire the key" is the key step, and `expect` names it (`has_matching_key`, in the first `Precedence`); `key_found` would add nothing, since the facts page says the key is never held before it is seen; "explore the side rooms" and "return to the corridor" have no label. Moved from KeyCorridorS6R3 to KeyCorridorS4R3 on 2026-11-20 (with cx-sequence): no method learned S6R3 in 71 runs. `expect` and the answer lists are unchanged. The S4R3 FARM bundle (production pair, `--reasoning max`, end judgment off: the default `reward_end_judgment`) adds Precedence(key_found, has_matching_key) beyond the card. That is on the LLM side: it read "find and acquire" as an order, and the user's rule is that only order words such as "then", "after" and "before" give an order. The scorer calls the clauses `mismatch`, so its training on S4R3 (FARM 2 of 3 seeds, no-RM 0 of 3) is kept as a probe only, not a benchmark result. The bundle is generated again after the card is updated for the user's stated-order rule. ARM-FM, 2026-11-20: the ARM-FM bundle still has the S6R3 page and room geometry; `run-suite` refuses it (bundle level mismatch), and it is generated again at the freeze. Stated-order rule 2026-11-20 (user): the plain list gives facts, but the compound "find and acquire the key" states an order (taking the key needs finding it first; user: "this one is fine"), so `expect` is Precedence(key_found, has_matching_key) with one Existence per fact, the ordered chain with that Precedence is the only `also_ok` answer, `forced` is gone, and the S4R3 FARM bundle above is correct and not generated again: its training counts (FARM 2 of 3 seeds, judged success 0.85, 0.82, 0.00 at 1.5M steps; no-RM 0 of 3).
